label: Syndrome decoding (binary, full-distance exponent)
problem: Selected classical upper bounds for decoding random binary linear codes at full Gilbert-Varshamov distance: for each algorithm, maximize its optimized time exponent over code rate R = k/n, with relative error weight H_2^{-1}(1-R). The coefficient c describes time 2^(c n + o(n)). The maximizing rate can change between algorithms; this is not a fixed-rate or fixed-code-instance comparison.

reference.label: n = 1346; worst-over-rate full-distance index
reference.why: 1346 is 128/0.0951 rounded to the nearest integer, so the selected corrected endpoint has c*n = 128.0046. This is an arbitrary normalization of an asymptotic exponent, not a claim of 128-bit security for a concrete code or deployed scheme. Each bound can attain its maximum at a different rate; no common rate, dimension, or error weight is fixed by this reference.

assumptions: Binary random linear codes; classical computation; full GV distance, not half-distance decoding; numerical optimization over algorithm parameters and then maximization over rate. The quoted asymptotic analyses and their distributional/list-size assumptions are accepted as stated. Polynomial factors, lower-order exponents, finite-size costs, and memory constraints are omitted. Exponential memory is allowed. Multiplying the rounded coefficient by n gives an index, not a calibrated operation count.
notes: The numeric series is deliberately limited to four sourced analyses from 2012 onward. It is not a complete history or a certification of the best attack as of 2026; omitted work and gaps between selected entries are not evidence of stability. Earlier ball-collision and representation work is retained as context without retrospectively dating coefficients from later comparison tables. Each year is the first public year of the quoted analysis rather than automatically the proceedings year; algorithm_year records an older algorithm when applicable. The series includes only bounds that remain supported by the cited analyses, under their assumptions. It does not reconstruct what researchers believed at every historical date: the original Both-May 0.0885 claim is excluded, and the corrected 0.0951 analysis enters in 2022. Different papers round numerical optima differently, so differences in the last reported decimal are not precise measurements. All entries remain verified:false pending the separate human review.

milestones.name: Ball-collision decoding (historical context)
milestones.ref: Smaller decoding exponents: ball-collision decoding, ePrint 2010/585; CRYPTO 2011
milestones.assumptions: Asymptotic random-code analysis, with time-memory tradeoffs and parameters optimized for the chosen rate and error fraction.
milestones.notes: This is an exponential improvement, not merely a constant-factor improvement. No scalar coefficient is entered here because this selected numeric series starts with the directly quoted 2012 full-distance table. The date is the first ePrint posting, before the 2011 proceedings.

milestones.name: Representation technique (MMT; historical context)
milestones.ref: Decoding Random Linear Codes in O-tilde(2^(0.054 n)), ASIACRYPT 2011
milestones.assumptions: Random binary linear codes; representation-based information-set decoding with exponential memory.
milestones.notes: A precursor of BJMM. The exponent in this paper's title and abstract concerns half-distance decoding and must not be used in the full-distance series. The later 2012 comparison table reports a full-distance MMT coefficient, which is not backdated here.

milestones.name: BJMM full-distance analysis
milestones.ref: Decoding Random Binary Linear Codes in 2^(n/20): How 1+1=0 Improves Information Set Decoding, ePrint 2012/026, Table 1; EUROCRYPT 2012
milestones.assumptions: Table 1 full-decoding time column: maximize the optimized coefficient over 0 < R < 1. Optimize for time rather than a common memory budget; omit lower-order costs.
milestones.notes: The selected series begins here. The same table's half-distance coefficient is 0.04934; it is not the value used in this series.

milestones.name: Nearest-neighbor decoding (May-Ozerov)
milestones.ref: On Computing Nearest Neighbors with Applications to Decoding of Binary Linear Codes, EUROCRYPT 2015, Theorem 3 and Figure 1
milestones.assumptions: Full-distance worst-over-rate asymptotic analysis using the nearest-neighbor routine and representation technique; accept the paper's list-distribution model and omit hidden factors.
milestones.notes: Uses the 0.097 coefficient explicitly printed in this primary paper, without adding unsupported decimal precision. This asymptotic bound is not an implementation cost estimate; see the 2025 context entry.

milestones.name: BJMM with nearest neighbors
milestones.ref: Optimizing BJMM with Nearest Neighbors: Full Decoding in 2^(2n/21) and McEliece Security, WCC 2017; prior bound reported in ePrint 2017/1139
milestones.assumptions: Full-distance worst-over-rate asymptotic analysis; exponential-memory list algorithms and nearest-neighbor assumptions; lower-order factors suppressed.
milestones.notes: This is the prior BJMM-nearest-neighbor bound reported by Both-May. It is distinct from their subsequently corrected 0.0885 claim in the same year.

milestones.name: Original Both-May 0.0885 claim (subsequently corrected)
milestones.ref: Decoding Linear Codes with High Error Rate and its Impact for LPN Security, ePrint 2017/1139; PQCrypto 2018
milestones.assumptions: Historical claim only. Its original list-size analysis was flawed, so the claimed exponent is not accepted as a supported bound.
milestones.notes: The original paper claimed a full-distance coefficient of 0.0885. Carrier et al. identified the error in 2022, and Esser supplied a detailed corrected analysis. The 0.0885 value is deliberately excluded from the numeric series; see the 2022 correction. The first public posting was in 2017, although the proceedings appeared in 2018.

milestones.name: RLPN decoding and identification of the Both-May error
milestones.ref: Statistical Decoding 2.0: Reducing Decoding to LPN, arXiv:2208.02201, Appendix B; ASIACRYPT 2022
milestones.assumptions: RLPN uses a reduction to LPN and the distributional assumptions stated in the paper. Its rate-dependent improvements are not entered as a single worst-over-rate coefficient here.
milestones.notes: RLPN improves over ISD at low rates, around R <= 0.3. The paper also identifies the invalid Both-May list-size estimate. A hoped-for or genie-aided low-rate limit is not an achieved algorithm and is not included in the series.

milestones.name: Corrected Both-May analysis
milestones.authors: Esser; following the correction by Carrier et al.
milestones.ref: Revisiting Nearest-Neighbor-Based Information Set Decoding, ePrint 2022/1328; also tabulated in Ducas et al., Asymptotics and Improvements of Sieving for Codes, Table 1
milestones.assumptions: Corrected full-GV-distance worst-over-rate analysis with nearest-neighbor/list assumptions and exponential memory. The exponent is a rounded numerical optimum; suppressed terms are not calibrated.
milestones.notes: The corrected coefficient is about 0.0951, not 0.0885. It is assigned to the 2022 analysis rather than backdated to the original 2017 algorithm. The later Ducas et al. comparison places the maximizing rate near 0.42, illustrating why this series must not be described as fixed rate 1/2. This is the endpoint of the selected series, not a claim of an exhaustive latest frontier.

milestones.name: Double-RLPN (rate-dependent improvement)
milestones.ref: Reduction from sparse LPN to LPN, Dual Attack 3.0, arXiv:2312.00747; EUROCRYPT 2024
milestones.assumptions: Rate-dependent random-code analysis under the paper's reduction and decoding assumptions; no single scalar worst-over-rate bound is extracted for this dataset.
milestones.notes: Extends the range of rates at which the proposed method improves over previous methods to approximately R <= 0.42. It was first public in December 2023. Its omission from the scalar series does not mean there was no progress in decoding after 2022.

milestones.name: Sieving for codes and comparison of corrected bounds
milestones.ref: Asymptotics and Improvements of Sieving for Codes, Table 1, CWI publication 33753
milestones.assumptions: Full-GV-distance worst-case rates are optimized separately for each algorithm; time and memory are separately tabulated.
milestones.notes: Table 1 lists Prange at about R=0.45 with c=0.1207, BJMM at about R=0.43 with c=0.1020, and corrected Both-May at about R=0.42 with c=0.0951. The sieving variants in this table do not lower the selected scalar endpoint. These comparisons corroborate the varying-rate interpretation rather than supply a fixed-code security estimate.

milestones.name: Concrete limitations of the May-Ozerov nearest-neighbor routine
milestones.ref: The May-Ozerov Algorithm for Syndrome Decoding is Galactic, IACR Communications in Cryptology 2(1), 2025
milestones.assumptions: Concrete analysis of the asymptotic nearest-neighbor subroutine, including costs suppressed in a leading-exponent comparison.
milestones.notes: Shows that the asymptotic nearest-neighbor advantage can require enormous code lengths before becoming useful. This reinforces the limitation of c*n as a leading-term index; it is not a finite-parameter work estimate or an implementation benchmark.
